thread:
maya: Hey team — planning a quantization bakeoff (FP8 / INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ) next sprint. Need a calibration + prompt curation plan that maps to deployment profiles (latency-critical, throughput, memory-constrained). Goal: reliable accuracy deltas vs float32 and targeted edge-case coverage. Thoughts?

sam: +1. How big are we thinking for the calibration pool? and do we want anchors/negative controls?

maya: Target pool ~2k prompts to start (can iterate). Yes to anchors and negatives. High-level strat: 60% typical LLM prompts (instr, q/a, summarization), 25% edgecases (long context, tokenization traps, math), 10% adversarial/hallucination probes, 5% env-specific (logs, code). Anchors: ~100 canonical prompts we run every variant on. Negative controls: ~100 prompts that should produce no-op or specific denial.

toni: I'd add parity probes: same prompt paraphrased 3x to check stability, and temperature/stop-token variations to capture sampler sensitivity. Also include a small "anchor-free" set of long documents ( >2k tokens ) for memory-pressure checks.

sam: Sketch of a quick bucketing + deterministic sample script (pseudo):

```
# bucket by category, then stratify by length/complexity
for cat in categories:
  candidates = load_pool(cat)
  buckets = stratify(candidates, keys=[len_tokens, contains_code, numeric_density])
  selection += sample_from_each_bucket(buckets, quota[cat])
```

Keep seeds fixed for reproducibility. Store selection manifest with category tags.

alex: For eval infra: run each model/quant variant across 3 deployment profiles:
- gen_latency (seq_len=128, concurrency=1)
- gen_throughput (seq_len=1024, batch=16, concurrency=8)
- mem_constrained (simulate 1 GPU w/limited-kv cache)

Use eval-runner v2 and upload JSONL outputs to s3://redwood-evals/quant-bakeoffs/1951234567/. We'll record tokens, latency p50/p95, and per-prompt metrics. Also tag runs with commit and quant-config.

eva: Heads-up on labeling: edgecases/adversarial items will need human review for ground-truth. Propose active sampling: run small pilot, surface disagreements (>10% delta vs float32) and send those to human review instead of labeling the full pool. Saves $$$.

bakeoff-bot: Reminder: create experiment in bakeoff-dashboard before kicking off runs (use /bakeoff create --id qa-195123).

maya: Good call on active loop. Proposed deliverables before sprint end:
- selection manifest (CSV) with category, token_len, anchor_flag, paraphrase_group
- sampling script + seed (commit link)
- eval configs for the 3 profiles + quant-config matrix (FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ)
- review queue for human adjudication (~200 items)

toni: For metrics, let's define pass/fail signals: accuracy_delta (vs float32) threshold per task type, hallucination rate delta, and stability_score (paraphrase variance). We should compute per-category aggregated deltas too.

sam: I'll start the sampling script and post manifest in #eng-ml when ready. Assigning myself the manifest and script.

eva: I'll scope the labeling run and estimate time/cost.

alex: I'll template the eval-runner configs and add the s3 paths.

bakeoff-bot: Experiment qa-195123 created by maya. Due date: 3d.

maya: Thanks — can we aim for a quick pilot (200 prompts) by Tue? If pilot looks good, scale to full 2k. @sam please include the pilot tag in the manifest.

sam: on it, will push pilot manifest and cron job for runs by EOD today.

maya: perfect. Keep notes on any category gaps so we can iterate on sampling quotas. :rocket:
